findings.title: Exclude successfully scheduled reminders from retry cleanup
findings.body: The retry-count branch deletes reminders regardless of their scheduled status. If overlapping cron invocations load an unscheduled reminder with retryCount = 1, one can successfully store scheduled = true and the Twilio reference while the other fails and writes retryCount = 2. The next invocation then deletes the successfully scheduled reminder even though its send date is still in the future. Twilio's message remains queued, but its reference is lost, preventing subsequent cancellation or rescheduling. Restrict exhausted-retry cleanup to reminders that are still unscheduled.

findings.title: Increment retryCount atomically instead of using the batch snapshot
findings.body: Both failure paths assign reminder.retryCount + 1 using the value fetched before processing the batch. If two cron invocations load retryCount = 0 and both fail, both write 1, so two failed attempts are recorded as only one and the reminder is attempted again instead of being retired. Repeated overlaps similarly undercount failures. Use Prisma's atomic increment operation in both failure paths so concurrent failures are not lost.

findings.title: Keep failure bookkeeping from escaping the per-reminder catch
findings.body: If another cron invocation's cleanup deletes a reminder after this invocation loads its batch, updating that reminder raises Prisma's record-not-found error. The catch now attempts another update against the same deleted ID, and that rejection is unhandled. Consequently, one stale reminder aborts the entire request and leaves all later reminders unprocessed, whereas the previous catch logged the error and continued. Handle missing rows or separately guard the retry-count write so it cannot terminate the batch.
